A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same informed asymmetric actor-critic work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including reliable matching of relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original reinforcement-learning experiments and synthetic POMDP analyses of signal informativeness, observation noise and feature selection.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices F–G retain original empirical results and add POPGym experiments and wall-clock measurements.

M1.justification: The history-dependent actor, privileged-signal critic, TD learning and two informativeness tests remain unchanged. Feature-subset, encoding and expert-signal discussions elaborate the existing framework. The revised permutation formula matches the procedure already specified in v2's Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: v3 adds six POPGym tasks: Higher Lower, Repeat First, Repeat Previous, Count Recall, Concentration and Position Cart Pole. These substantially extend coverage into card-memory and partially observed balancing tasks. All six navigation benchmarks and the synthetic POMDP scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The shared navigation experiments retain A2C, asym-A2C-s and asym-A2C-hs; synthetic experiments retain the symmetric baseline. POPGym reuses A2C and the history-state comparator. Expert actions are privileged critic inputs, not a separately evaluated expert-policy baseline.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a POPGym protocol with two million environment steps, 256-unit GRUs and backpropagation truncation length 1,024, and adds AUC as an evaluation metric. Existing navigation and synthetic training settings are retained. Figure 2 changes its stated smoothing units to environment steps without reconciling the retained gradient-step description.

E4.justification: v3 expands signal-choice analyses to expert cues, card-memory features and separate velocity components in POPGym, and adds computational-cost comparisons in Appendix F. The earlier synthetic signal-choice, observation-noise and alternative-observation analyses remain in G.2–G.4.

E5.justification: Figure 2 changes from mean-only curves to means with standard-deviation bands across the same ten runs. The existing twenty-run benchmark and ten-run synthetic reporting practices remain, without a documented increase in repeated runs or a new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds POPGym results, synthetic AUC values in Table 1 and wall-clock measurements in Tables 3–5. Figure 2 also revises the plotted mean curves. Original informativeness statistics are unchanged, including v2 Tables 3–5, now Tables 7–9. Conflicting POPGym values and rankings between Figure 1 and Table 6 limit interpretation of those additions.

T1.justification: The central unbiasedness results are retained. v3 adds history conditioning to Equation 6, replaces state variance with return variance in Section 3.1, and explicitly states an integrability assumption in the policy-gradient proof. Appendix C.2 retains the L2 perturbation bound but removes v2's rejection-threshold inequalities, HSIC bandwidth argument and asymptotic-power discussion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: arbitrary state-dependent privileged signals, unbiased policy gradients, two informativeness criteria, and partial signals that can match or outperform full-state critics. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations involving value aliasing, shared stationary conditions and expert signals, explicitly discusses test-calibration risks from regression error, and introduces a discussion of task-dependent selection and irrelevant features as structured noise. These extend the earlier return-relevance and variance explanations.

D1.justification: New appendices document POPGym signals, preprocessing, architectures and hyperparameters, plus extensive runtime information. Reported hardware changes from 64 cores/72 GB RAM to 96 cores/93.75 GB RAM. The code URL is unchanged. Count Recall's signal descriptions disagree with Tables 4 and 6, limiting reproducibility of that addition.

R1.justification: v3 adds POPGym, Cart Pole and recent robotics references, plus causal decision-making papers by Lee and Bareinboim and Lu et al. The introduction distinguishes statistical signal selection from approaches requiring causal models. The central positioning relative to earlier asymmetric actor-critic work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract, introduction, signal-selection passage and conclusion, moves three unbiasedness lemmas from Section 3.1 to Appendix A, and reorganizes appendix subsections. A discussion subsection is added, while the six main sections and much of the retained exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one column to two columns with new typography and headers. Figure 1 expands from six to twelve rearranged panels; Figure 2 gains uncertainty bands and revised axes and legends. Table 1 gains an AUC column, four tables are added, and retained appendix tables are reformatted and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful benchmark breadth, runtime information, uncertainty bands and mathematical refinements. However, its new POPGym evidence contains unresolved contradictions: Figure 1(k) and Section 5.1 portray the full-state Concentration critic as inferior, whereas Table 6 reports its highest mean return, 0.424 versus 0.259 for the best partial signal, with unexplained scale and ranking differences. Signal descriptions also conflict with reported comparisons. These problems affect the major added validation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
